In a little over a decade Congress created the National Security Council, the CIA, the Air Force, and a single Department of Defense, then gave that department a working chain of command. It also wrote one code of military justice, a standing draft law, and a tool for mobilizing industry. These are framework statutes: most later laws plug into the institutions they created.

## What you should be able to do

- Describe what the National Security Act of 1947 created and what the 1949 and 1958 amendments fixed.
- Explain why the operational chain of command bypasses the military departments.
- Identify the Korean War era statutes still used today.

## Reading path

Read these in order. Each card links to the wiki page and to the official text. Ticking a box saves your progress in this browser only.

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="nsa-1947"}
[National Security Act](../../statutes/nsa-1947.qmd) [1947]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

The founding charter of the modern national security system. It created the National Security Council and the Central Intelligence Agency, established a separate Air Force, and placed the military departments under a single Secretary of Defense.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/61/495), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/3002?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="nsa-1947"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-defense-arms data-statute="nsa-amendments-1949"}
[NSA Amendments (1949)](../../statutes/nsa-amendments-1949.qmd) [1949]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

Fixed the weak structure created in 1947. It turned the National Military Establishment into the Department of Defense, an executive department, and reduced the Army, Navy, and Air Force to military departments under the Secretary of Defense.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/63/578), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/10/111?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="nsa-amendments-1949"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="cia-act-1949"}
[CIA Act](../../statutes/cia-act-1949.qmd) [1949]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

Gave the CIA the administrative tools to operate in secret: authority to spend money without the usual accounting rules, to withhold information about its staff and structure, and to procure and transfer funds confidentially.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/63/208), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/3501?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="cia-act-1949"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-defense-arms data-statute="dod-reorg-1958"}
[DoD Reorganization Act (1958)](../../statutes/dod-reorg-1958.qmd) [1958]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

President Eisenhower's reorganization. It took the military departments out of the operational chain of command, so that orders run from the President and the Secretary of Defense to unified commands, and it confirmed the Secretary's authority, direction, and control over the whole department.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/72/514), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/10/162?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="dod-reorg-1958"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-defense-arms data-statute="ucmj-1950"}
[UCMJ](../../statutes/ucmj-1950.qmd) [1950]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

The criminal code and court system of the U.S. armed forces. It replaced the separate Army and Navy disciplinary codes with one law for all services, defining military offenses, the types of courts-martial, the rights of the accused, and civilian appellate review.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/64/107), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/10/801?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="ucmj-1950"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-defense-arms data-statute="dpa-1950"}
[Defense Production Act](../../statutes/dpa-1950.qmd) [1950]{.reading-year} [Partly expired]{.status .status-partly-expired} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

A Korean War statute that lets the President direct private industry in the interest of national defense: by putting government orders first in line, by financing new production capacity, and by organizing industry cooperation.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/64/798), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/4501?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="dpa-1950"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-defense-arms data-statute="selective-service-1948"}
[Selective Service Act](../../statutes/selective-service-1948.qmd) [1948]{.reading-year} [Partly expired]{.status .status-partly-expired} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

The standing law of conscription. It requires men to register at 18 and maintains the Selective Service System so that a draft could be run if Congress and the President restored the power to induct.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/62/604), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/3801?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="selective-service-1948"> I have read this</label>
:::

## Further reading

- [Smith-Mundt Act](../../statutes/smith-mundt-1948.qmd){.subj}: The legal foundation of U.S. public diplomacy. It authorized the State Department to explain the United States to foreign audiences through broadcasting, publications, and educational and cultural exchanges.
- [Lend-Lease Act](../../statutes/lend-lease-1941.qmd){.subj}: Authorized the President to sell, transfer, lend, or lease defense articles to any country whose defense he judged vital to the defense of the United States.
- [Mutual Security Act](../../statutes/mutual-security-1951.qmd){.subj}: Merged the Marshall Plan's economic aid, military assistance to allies, and technical assistance into one program under one agency, with the stated purpose of strengthening the free world against Soviet power.
- [Atomic Energy Act](../../statutes/aea-1954.qmd){.subj}: The governing law for both civilian and military uses of nuclear material in the United States.

## Key terms

**Framework statute**
:   A standing law that creates an institution or a general procedure that later laws and executive actions depend on.

**Operational chain of command**
:   The line of authority for military operations, which since 1958 runs from the President through the Secretary of Defense to the unified commands, not through the service departments.

**Unified combatant command**
:   A command with forces from more than one service under a single commander, organized by region or function.

## Check yourself

Try to answer each question before opening it.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 1. Name three things the National Security Act of 1947 created.

The National Security Council, the Central Intelligence Agency, and a separate Air Force, with the military departments placed under a single Secretary of Defense. See [National Security Act](../../statutes/nsa-1947.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 2. What did the 1949 amendments change?

They turned the loose National Military Establishment into the Department of Defense, an executive department, and reduced the Army, Navy, and Air Force to military departments under the Secretary. See [NSA Amendments (1949)](../../statutes/nsa-amendments-1949.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 3. What did the 1958 reorganization do to the operational chain of command?

It took the military departments out of it, so that orders run from the President and Secretary of Defense to the unified commands. See [DoD Reorganization Act (1958)](../../statutes/dod-reorg-1958.qmd), and later [Goldwater-Nichols Act](../../statutes/goldwater-nichols-1986.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 4. Which Korean War statute lets the government put defense orders first in line at private companies?

The [Defense Production Act](../../statutes/dpa-1950.qmd), which also finances new production capacity and organizes industry cooperation. Parts of it depend on periodic reauthorization.
:::
